newsitem.title: ROMANIA: US Bell Helicopter to buy stake in Romanian firm.
newsitem.headline: US Bell Helicopter to buy stake in Romanian firm.

text.p: U.S. firm Bell Helicopter Textron said on Wednesday it would buy a 70 percent stake in Romanian aircraft maker Intreprinderea Aeronautica Romana (IAR) and the Defence Ministry said it would buy 96 helicopters to be made in the Balkan country.
A statement issued at the signing ceremony in Bucharest said Bell was acquiring 70 percent of the firm, with the remaining 30 percent going to public shareholders.
It said the aim of the purchase was to co-produce AH-1RO "Dracula" attack helicopters, a Romanian version of the twin-engine AH-1W Super Cobra aircraft used by U.S. marines.
The Defence Ministry immediately said it had signed a contract to purchase 96 of the craft to be produced at IAR's plant in Brasov, north of Bucharest.
Sorin Dimitriu, president of State Ownership Fund, the body responsible for overseeing the privatisation of state companies in Romania, said the project would cost "billions of dollars".
Earlier estimates had put the cost of the project at $1 billion.
The Textron statement said the Brasov plant would "serve as a manufacturing source for Bell Helicopter and other Textron divisions in Eastern Europe".
The accord, which implies sensitive technology transfers, remained subject to approval by the U.S. State Department and the Textron board of directors.
The Defence Ministry announcement said the air frame would be produced in Brasov and the engine by the Romanian firm Turbomecanica SA in conjunction with General Electric of the United States.
The avionics will be produced by AE Electronics, a joint venture between a local aircraft maker and Elbit Systems Limited of Israel.
